title: Go: Nil Slice & Map
description: Write a Go program that demonstrates nil slices and maps and how to safely work with them.

codeTemplate.go:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var s []int
	var m map[string]int

	fmt.Println("nil slice len:", len(s))
	fmt.Println("nil slice == nil:", s == nil)
	fmt.Println("nil map len:", len(m))
	fmt.Println("nil map == nil:", m == nil)

	s = append(s, 10)
	fmt.Println("appended slice:", s)

	m = make(map[string]int)
	m["a"] = 1
	fmt.Println("map after init:", m["a"])
}

verificationTest: output.includes('nil slice len: 0') && output.includes('nil slice == nil: true') && output.includes('appended slice: [10]') && output.includes('map after init: 1')
hints: A nil slice has length 0 and is safe to use with append
A nil map has length 0 but assigning to a nil map causes a panic
Use `make()` to initialize a map before adding elements
